categories.name: Live Data Activation (waiting on the tournament)

items.title: Real 2026 player stats via API-Football
items.detail: Switch player_source to apifootball once the 2026 World Cup squads are populated by API-Football (currently 0 players this far out). This replaces the EA FC 26 stand-in ratings with real per-player match stats feeding the percentile PPS engine. A free key + the 12h throttle are already wired; set apifootball_season=2022 to demo the real scoring path now.

items.title: Kalshi WC markets go live
items.detail: Kalshi has no World Cup markets listed yet — they open closer to/during the tournament. fetch_kalshi() already self-heals by auto-discovering the live series ticker, so the live odds + model-vs-market edge fill in automatically once markets appear. Verify the discovered series and title parsing against the real markets when they list.

items.title: Calibrate p-from-combined mapping
items.detail: The per-match win probability uses a fixed linear map p = 0.30 + combined/100·0.45 (clamped 0.05-0.97). Backtest it against historical results (e.g. the 2022 season via API-Football) and calibrate the slope/intercept so p is empirically grounded rather than assumed.

items.title: Surface squad-score confidence
items.detail: SSS already carries a confidence (conf) from minutes coverage and metric richness, but the betting window doesn't show it. Expose confidence next to the window so a low-data team's number is visibly less trustworthy.

items.title: Head-to-head / draw modelling
items.detail: The model treats each match as a single win probability for one team. Extend toward an explicit win/draw/loss split (relevant for group-stage points and knockout 'advance' probabilities) so the standings projection and bracket survival are modelled, not just per-match p.

items.title: QI Brain session + decision logging
items.detail: Register Gamez sessions and notable decisions (model tweaks, data-source switches, betting-window readings) in the QI Brain via qi.log_session()/qi.log_decision() for cross-project memory. Not yet wired — Gamez is registered in qi_registry.json but doesn't call the Brain.

items.title: QI Standards compliance audit
items.detail: Run qi_validator.py --project gamez. Confirm the 7-folder QI layout (engine/config/data/logs/tests/docs/tools), per-project engine/bin/nssm.exe, and that LOGS/docs locations match QI_Standards.md. The proxy currently lives flat under proxy/ rather than the standard layout.

items.title: Mission Control health tile
items.detail: Expose Gamez's /health (source, fixtures/teams/players counts, next_refresh_s, openrouter/live_stats flags) on the QI Hive Mission Control board so its liveness is visible alongside the other services.

items.title: Publish the GitHub repo
items.detail: qi_registry.json lists github: TBD. Create the repo and wire the existing .github/workflows/build.yml so the cross-OS artifacts publish on tag, giving friends a clean download page instead of hand-shared zips.

items.title: Code-sign the Windows build
items.detail: The unsigned PyInstaller .exe trips antivirus/EDR (hence the /allowlist-info SHA-256 helper and Defender-exclusion command). Code-signing the binary would remove most of that friction for non-technical friends.

items.title: macOS / Linux build verification
items.detail: CI produces mac and linux binaries but they're built on runners, not verified end-to-end. Smoke-test the pywebview window + proxy boot on a real mac and linux box before treating those artifacts as release-ready.

items.title: Rate-limit the shared AI over the tunnel
items.detail: The shared OpenRouter AI is gated only by an optional access code. Add per-IP rate limiting on /ai/openrouter so a shared link can't exhaust the free-tier quota, complementing the existing password gate and free-model fallback.

items.title: Cache freshness / staleness signalling
items.detail: The page shows as_of and source, but a long ESPN/Kalshi outage silently serves old cache. Add an explicit staleness badge (e.g. as_of older than 2× refresh_minutes) so users know when they're looking at last-good data.
